[quote=bantarus;58984275]A gust of cold wind rolled in from the sea, carrying the scent of brine, metal, and the ever-present tang of fuel from the massive harbor machinery. The Jomslandic delegation observed Legatus Marcus Junius Silvanus and his men with a mixture of curiosity and quiet amusement. The golden armor gleamed under the overcast sky, an anachronism amidst the modern setting of steel, concrete, and the hum of engines. Dockworkers and bystanders cast glances toward the arriving warriors, some exchanging murmured words, others simply being impressed by the traditional armor which in Jomslands only gets worn during festivities and such.
Jarl Freyderic, a man of diplomacy, maintained a neutral expression, but General Hjalmarsson raised an eyebrow behind his sunglasses. He had seen many visiting dignitaries, but never one so clad in the splendor of antiquity. If the legatus felt out of place in this world of high-tech weaponry, mechanized warfare, and modern infrastructure, he did not show it.  
Freyderic returned the salute with a respectful nod. Our People value punctuality, but we also understand the sea can be unforgiving. You arrived safely, and that is what matters.  
Beside him, General Hjalmarsson finally spoke, his voice low and measured. Your armor is impressive. A fine work of craftsmanship. But I suspect it offers little protection against modern weaponry. He gestured subtly to the Jomslandic military personnel nearby, clad in ballistic vests, modern stabproof chainmail and carrying sleek automatic rifles. His words were not mocking, merely an observation, a warrior acknowledging another warrior, albeit from vastly different eras.  
Jarl Freyderic smoothly redirected the conversation. Come. Our capital awaits. Your delegation will be received by the High King and the Althing. We have arranged accommodations, and should you require anything, do not hesitate to ask.  
He gestured toward the convoy of waiting SUVs and military vehicles, their engines rumbling softly. Around them, the port continued its daily routine, container cranes towering above like iron giants, cargo ships unloading under the watchful eyes of dockworkers, and the distant wail of a foghorn echoing over the bay.  
For Legatus Marcus and his men, it was a world both alien and familiar. The scent of salt on the air was the same, the sea breeze unchanged, but this was not Versia, nor any battlefield of old. This was Jomsland, a land where past and present stood side by side, and where warriors still walked, but with rifles slung over their shoulders, not swords at their hips.  [/quote]

[i]The sights and smells would be almost overwheimg, yet the Legatus would be unphased yet mystified. Marcus acknowledge General Hjalmarsson's words, giving a bow. "Your words bring us honor. We take pride in our service as soldiers. Please, after you." He allow the Jarl and his generals and delegates to lead the way. He would walk and talk with them, and converse as they travelled in the SUVs and military vehicles.[/i]

[i]"My Lords, please don't be fooled my arms and armor. We are trained and battle-hardened in the arts of modern warfare, and have seen the blood and death caused not by spear and bow like in times of old, but by rifle and artillery. At home, we have much more advanced armor than just these traditional garments of a bygone Era. My soldiers equip this, if you take a closer look. I will provide an inspection of my Legion once we arrive, should you be interested." Once they reached the SUVs and military vehicles, he would continue. "We possess modern, fully reinforced iron and steel suits capable of stopping small-arms fire and offering strong protection across all areas of the Versian body. We have buildings of steel and glass, forges that that turn iron, gold, and even steel to dust, fortresses of concrete and railguns (railway naval guns set on tracks) that can stop and decimate infantry and armor with precise accuracy. We are a nation built for war using the advancements and innovations of our previous Era, known as the Industrial Age." The Jarl would see that this was true, as Marcus had only a pistol strapped on his back, beside his ceremonial Gladius. His soldiers carried reinforced ironsteel shields and SMGs slung across their backs, with packs of ammunition around their waists. They also wore said fully-encased iron suits, their faces covered by custom-made masks of Emperor Honorious and other important historical figures.

"I only ask my men are given provisions to eat and a place to rest their heads after their long journey."[/i]

As the Versian spoke of his homelands industrial might, of railguns, steel towers, and the devastation of modern war, the General listened without interruption. His men did the same, their hardened faces betraying no reaction. When Marcus finished, Hjalmarsson gave a curt nod.
"It seems we misjudged have misjudged you. Perhaps our people arent so different after all. the General said in a measured tone.
The SUVs rumbled to life, their engines echoing through the streets as the delegation set off towards Bondahall. Along the way, the Legatus and his men would see the stark contrast of Jomsland, rows of houses and halls built in ancient styles stood beside modern factories and shipyards. Police Officers in modern vehicles patrolled the streets, while other people in furs and mail trained in open courtyards with blades and bows.
"Your men have traveled far, and in Jomsland, guests are treated with the respect they have earned. Food and shelter will be provided, and your soldiers will have time to rest and recover from their journey," he said, his voice warm. "And should you wish it, we would be honored to witness the strength of your Legion with our own eyes. We value words, but we value deeds even more."
